title: Drying, curing, storage, and water activity — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define the source-supported claims and evidence boundaries required before authoring the full controlled GROW-140 postharvest SOP package.

excludedUntilValidated: one universal room temperature or RH target
one universal product water-activity release threshold for every jurisdiction and product class
claims that curing can remediate contaminated material
shelf-life claims without product- and package-specific stability evidence

claims.statement: Drying rate and final product condition depend on interacting process variables including temperature, humidity, airflow, loading, flower geometry and time; room averages alone do not prove uniform product condition.
claims.boundary: A room setpoint is a process input, not direct evidence that every location or flower in a lot reached the same condition.

claims.statement: Moisture content and water activity describe different properties of dried plant material and should not be treated as interchangeable indicators.
claims.boundary: A measured moisture percentage cannot by itself establish microbial or chemical stability, and a water-activity result must be interpreted with method, temperature, sampling and applicable specification.

claims.statement: Cannabis/hemp drying methods can alter drying time, decarboxylation, color, microbial load, cannabinoid form and volatile retention, creating quality and safety tradeoffs rather than one universally superior method.
claims.boundary: Results from a specific cultivar, apparatus or drying treatment must not be converted directly into a universal cannabis recipe.

claims.statement: Curing and sealed storage can change product moisture condition after drying, so sealed packaging does not eliminate the need for representative product measurements and stability checks.
claims.boundary: Curing is not a validated remediation method for unsafe microbial contamination or materially nonconforming product.

claims.statement: Storage stability is influenced by time, temperature, oxygen, light, humidity/moisture transfer, product matrix and packaging properties, and these factors can affect cannabinoids and volatile compounds differently.
claims.boundary: Preserving one compound or using one package technology does not prove preservation of total product quality.

claims.statement: Cannabinoid degradation in dried cannabis is time- and temperature-dependent under studied conditions, supporting the need to justify storage specifications and shelf-life with measured stability evidence.
claims.boundary: Kinetic findings from a study are not a finished-product expiry date and cannot replace product-specific stability validation.

claims.statement: Representative sampling and lot traceability are necessary to investigate within-load variability, drying-room deviations and later storage failures without overgeneralizing from a convenience sample.
claims.boundary: A single favorable sample does not demonstrate uniformity across a heterogeneous lot.

claims.statement: Postharvest disposition should preserve lot identity, define actual exposure and affected scope, review product-condition and stability evidence, and document authorized release, hold, rework or rejection decisions.
claims.boundary: The SOP may define the evidence workflow but should not invent jurisdiction-specific release limits or override required laboratory and regulatory controls.

requiredNewPackageSections: drying endpoint and hold/review decision framework
lot genealogy, split/merge and movement records
